ety.text: From Ottoman in the early 19th century; so named because reclining on a couch was associated with Middle Eastern customs.

senses.d: An upholstered sofa, without arms or a back, sometimes with a compartment for storing linen etc.
ex: A 39-year-old British woman was killed when a malfunctioning ottoman bed fell on her neck and asphyxiated her, a coroner’s report said.

senses.d: A low stool or thick cushion used to rest the feet or as a seat.
ex: This ottoman is set on casters, and is a great convenience for holding articles, while serving also as a seat.

senses.d: A fabric with a pronounced ribbed or corded effect, often made of silk or a mixture of cotton and silk-like yarns.

ety.text: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish دیوان (dîvân), from Persian دیوان (divân).

pt:pufe.gl: beanbag (a large covering stuffed with pellets used as furniture)
